items.title: Firmonertinib in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with epidermal growth factor receptor P-loop and αC-helix compressing mutations.
items.abstract: P-loop and αC-helix compressing (PACC) mutations comprise a structurally distinct subgroup of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with limited treatment options. Firmonertinib is a once-daily oral, brain-penetrant, mutant-selective EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor with a unique trifluoroethoxy side chain. Firmonertinib had high anti-proliferative efficacy in EGFR PACC-mutant cells and xenografts. In the phase 1b FURTHER study (NCT05364073), patients with metastatic EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC randomized to receive first-line firmonertinib 160 mg (n = 25) or 240 mg (n = 22) had confirmed objective response rates (ORRs) of 43% and 68%, median duration of response not reached and 14.6 months, and median progression-free survival of 11.1 and 16.0 months, respectively; treatment-related adverse events led to dose reductions (19% and 24%) and discontinuation (3% and 0%). Intracranial ORR among patients with brain metastases at baseline was 47% (8/17). Results support further study of first-line firmonertinib in patients with EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC.

items.title: Initial HIV Therapy for Adults and Treatment-Associated Weight Gain: The Opti-DOR Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Antiretroviral therapy (ART), particularly regimens containing tenofovir alafenamide with dolutegravir or bictegravir, is associated with substantial weight gain, potentially exacerbating cardiometabolic risk in people with HIV.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a regimen with doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate results in less weight gain than a regimen with dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide while maintaining noninferior viral suppression.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, noninferiority randomized clinical trial including ART-naive adults (≥18 years of age) with an HIV RNA level greater than 500 copies/mL and no detectable baseline, high-level doravirine resistance. The study was conducted at 2 South African sites and individuals were recruited between October 2023 and March 2025. The final participant visit occurred in February 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: A once-daily regimen with 100 mg of doravirine, 300 mg of lamivudine, and 300 mg of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (n = 299) or 50 mg of dolutegravir, 200 mg of emtricitabine, and 25 mg of tenofovir alafenamide (n = 301).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was viral suppression (HIV RNA level <50 copies/mL) at week 48 (prespecified noninferiority margin of -10 percentage points). The key secondary outcomes included changes in body weight, treatment-associated effects on body composition, and safety and adverse events.
RESULTS: Among 600 participants, 597 (99.5%) were Black African, 413 (68.8%) were assigned female at birth, and the median age was 34 years (IQR, 28-41). At week 48, 266 participants (89.0%) in the doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate group achieved viral suppression (HIV RNA level <50 copies/mL) vs 273 participants (90.7%) in the dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide group (between-group difference, -1.7 percentage points [95% CI, -6.6 to 3.1], meeting the prespecified noninferiority margin of -10 percentage points). The median weight gain was 3.0 kg in the doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate group vs 5.0 kg in the dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide group (between-group difference, -2.0 kg [95% CI, -3.0 to -1.0 kg]; P < .001). Among participants in the doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate group, the median change in hip bone mineral density (BMD) was -2.1% (IQR, -4.1% to -0.5%) and was -3.2% (IQR, -5.4% to -0.8%) for spine BMD vs -0.5% (IQR, -1.9% to 1.2%) for hip BMD and -1.3% (IQR, -3.2% to 0.8%) for spine BMD with dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide (P < .001 for each between-group comparison). Resistance to doravirine emerged among 7 of 9 participants experiencing virologic failure in the doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate group. Of these 7 participants, 5 of 6 achieved viral suppression after switching to dolutegravir-based therapy and 1 was lost to follow-up. Serious adverse events and deaths (n = 2) were infrequent and not considered treatment-related.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among predominantly Black African adults initiating ART, a regimen with doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate was noninferior to a regimen with dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide for 48-week viral suppression and was associated with less weight gain.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05924438.

items.title: Individualized Cardiac Index-Guided Hemodynamic Therapy in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Elective Major Abdominal Surgery: The PELICAN Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: It remains unclear if intraoperative hemodynamic therapy should be guided by cardiac index.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy vs routine hemodynamic therapy improves outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days.
RESULTS: Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05648279.

items.title: Mifepristone Patient Agreement Form and Medication Abortion Knowledge: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: While the US Food and Drug Administration requires medication abortion patients to review and sign a patient agreement form (PAF) under its Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program, there is limited research examining whether the PAF improves patient knowledge.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether patients are more knowledgeable about medication abortion after reviewing and signing the PAF.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: People receiving mifepristone and misoprostol medications (15 years or older and proficient in English or Spanish) were recruited from 5 facilities in California, Colorado, Illinois, Kansas, and Minnesota (January to October 2025). After receiving standard clinic counseling and the mifepristone medication guide, patients were randomized into 2 study groups and then completed a survey either before (n = 301 control) or after (n = 292 exposed) receiving and signing the PAF. Data were analyzed December 2025 to August 2026.
INTERVENTION: The control group completed the survey before receiving the PAF and any PAF-related counseling. The exposed group received and signed the PAF and any PAF-related counseling and then completed a knowledge survey.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Overall medication abortion knowledge (correct response to 12 items regarding when to seek medical care, effectiveness, administration, potential serious risks, and side effects) and responses to each individual knowledge item.
RESULTS: A total of 593 participants (mean [SD] age, 26.9 [5.8] years; 44 Asian/Pacific Islander [7%], 132 Black [22%], 181 Hispanic [31%], and 159 White [27%] individuals) completed knowledge items (301 control [51%]; 292 exposed [49%]). Across participant characteristics, study groups only differed significantly in reported abortion history. In adjusted analyses, participants answered a mean (95% CI) of 10.37 (10.26-10.48) of 12 knowledge items consistently with the PAF with no study group differences (control: difference, 10.26; exposed: difference, 10.44; adjusted difference, 0.18; 95% CI, -0.04 to 0.39). Nearly everyone knew to contact a "provider" if they "were to have an infection (590 [99%]) or heavy bleeding that soaked through 2 full-size sanitary pads per hour for 2 hours (566 [96%])." The items with answers that were least often concordant with the PAF included how often the treatment does not work (320 [54%]) and taking misoprostol 24 to 48 hours after mifepristone (458 [77%]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The randomized clinical trial found that patient knowledge about medication abortion following standard counseling was high. Exposure to the required PAF did not result in a clinically meaningful increase in medication abortion knowledge. The findings raise questions about the PAF requirement from the US Food and Drug Administration, as it does not appear to be useful.

items.title: EGFR-targeted antibody-toxin conjugate in recurrent glioma: a phase 1 trial.
items.abstract: D2C7-ATC is a recombinant antibody-toxin conjugate (ATC) targeting wild-type epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and mutant EGFR variant III (EGFRvIII). We conducted a single-arm, single-site, open-label phase 1 trial evaluating a single infusion of D2C7-ATC via convection-enhanced delivery in the enhancing disease of 81 patients with biopsy-confirmed recurrent malignant glioma. The primary objective was to determine toxicity and the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of D2C7-ATC. Secondary objectives included describing overall survival (OS) and assessing the association between EGFR expression and OS. The median overall survival (mOS) was 7.9 months among 72 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type recurrent glioblastoma (IDHwt rGBM), including 35 patients in the dose-escalation stage (40 to 35,032 ng ml-1) and 37 patients in the dose-expansion stage (RP2D of 6,920 ng ml-1). D2C7-ATC was generally well tolerated, with mainly grade 1-2 treatment-related adverse events (67%). The maximum tolerated dose was exceeded at 35,032 ng ml-1, where four patients experienced dose-limiting toxicities, including grade 4 (N = 2) and grade 3 (N = 2) events. Eight patients died on trial; all deaths were unrelated to D2C7-ATC. Univariate analyses identified survival-associated biomarkers, including tumor D2C7 antibody reactivity, circulating cytokines, a tumor inflammatory gene signature and neutrophils, monocytes and lymphocytes in blood. Notably, patients with IDHwt rGBM with a D2C7 antibody reactivity score of <1.5+ in pre-treatment tumor had an mOS of 17.38 months, whereas those with low IL-8 in post-treatment plasma had an mOS of 16.6 months. These findings indicate that EGFR-targeted D2C7-ATC therapy prolongs survival in a subset of patients with IDHwt rGBM via intratumoral and systemic immune activation. items.title: Mobile Subthreshold Exercise Program (MSTEP) for Youth With Prolonged Concussion Recovery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Research suggests that aerobic exercise improves recovery for youth with concussion; however, prior studies primarily focused on acute concussion and required multiple in-person visits.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a virtually delivered aerobic exercise program improves recovery following concussion compared to a stretching control and examine potential moderators.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A randomized clinical trial was conducted from 2021 to 2025 comparing the Mobile Subthreshold Exercise Program (MSTEP) to a stretching control for 11- to 18-year-olds with concussion up to 1 year from injury. Participants were recruited from a variety of outpatient locations in 4 US states (Washington, Utah, Wisconsin, and Oregon). Recruitment and data collection occurred from March 2021 until October 2025, and data analysis occurred from November 2025 to April 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Youth randomized to MSTEP were provided activity trackers and an aerobic exercise program initiated at 60% of heart rate maximum. Exercise was advanced in intensity and duration over 6 weeks through weekly videoconferencing calls. Youth in the control group were given stretching exercises and similar weekly calls.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes included (1) concussive symptoms and (2) health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Secondary outcomes included sleep, depression, and anxiety. Moderation by sex, age, and time since injury was examined. Patients were followed up for 6 months.
RESULTS: The sample included 210 participants, among whom 122 (58.1%) were female, mean (SD) age was 15.1 (2.2) years, and mean (SD) time since injury was 73.3 (63.3) days. Covariate-adjusted regression analysis showed significant improvement in concussive symptoms and HRQoL at all time points, with greater improvement in MSTEP compared to control at the 3-month time point for both concussive symptoms (β, -3.15; 95% CI, -6.05 to -0.25; adjusted P = .04) and HRQoL (β, 4.15; 95% CI, 0.64-7.66; adjusted P = .04). No significant differences by group were seen at 6 months. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling with exponential decay showed significantly faster symptom recovery in MSTEP compared to control (difference in rates, -0.68; 95% CI, -2.22 to -0.04; P = .002). Secondary outcomes (sleep, depression, and anxiety) improved in all participants but were not different by group. Benefit of the intervention was only significant for individuals less than 3 months from injury (concussive symptoms: β, -4.44; 95% CI, -7.99 to -0.90; unadjusted P = .01; HRQoL: β, 6.64; 95% CI, 2.55-10.72; unadjusted P = .002). No evidence was found for moderation by other factors.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Per the results of this randomized clinical trial, an aerobic exercise program improves speed of recovery following concussion for youth compared to stretching and can be delivered remotely. However, this type of program appears to be most beneficial for individuals with acute or subacute injury (<3 months since injury).
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04688255.

items.title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women.
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

items.title: A randomized phase 2 study combining midostaurin, low-dose cytarabine and venetoclax in newly diagnosed AML ≥60 years.
items.abstract: In randomized studies, addition of FLT3 inhibitors failed to improve survival in older patients with FLT3-ITD AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy. Although hypomethylating agents or low-dose cytarabine combined with venetoclax is standard, FLT3-ITD is an important mechanism of resistance and a barrier to improved survival. Recent studies show promise for the addition of gilteritinib or quizartinib to less intensive venetoclax-based therapy, however resulting marrow toxicity requires substantial reductions to administered treatment. The INTERVENE study (Investigating Novel Triplets to Extend Remission with VENetoclax in Elderly AML) (ACTRN12619001655134) examined the role of midostaurin (M) administered sequentially after low-dose cytarabine (L) combined with venetoclax (V) in patients with newly diagnosed AML ≥60 years with non-adverse karyotype. After a run-in phase (n=18) established that LDAC combined with venetoclax from days 1-28 and midostaurin from days 11-28 was tolerable, 120 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive either LVM or LV. For the primary endpoint, LVM did not improve composite complete remission (CRc), compared to LV (72% vs 68%). Combining midostaurin with LV enhanced CRc among the sub-group of patients (n=29) with FLT3-ITD (82% vs 57%, difference = 25%, 0.85 posterior probability true difference > 5%, 95% CrI: -10 to 59%) and improved FLT3-ITD clearance as measured by ultrasensitive NGS (65% vs 0%), resulting in longer OS (median 24.2 vs 8.8 months, HR=0.34, 95% CrI: 0.071 to 0.960), compared to LV. In conclusion, midostaurin combined with low-dose cytarabine and venetoclax is well-tolerated and may have a role in newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy.

items.title: Effect of Aficamten on Cardiac Structure and Function in Patients With Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aficamten significantly improved both functional capacity and patient-reported health status in patients with symptomatic nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled ACACIA-HCM trial (Assessment Comparing Aficamten to Placebo on Cardiac Endpoints in Adults with Non-Obstructive HCM; NCT06081894). Serial echocardiographic examinations may provide insights into the mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effect of aficamten in this prespecified exploratory analysis.
METHODS: Symptomatic patients with nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy were randomized 1:1 to receive aficamten (range, 5-20 mg, titration based on left ventricular [LV] ejection fraction) or placebo for up to 72 weeks (end of treatment). The effect of aficamten on echocardiographic measures at 36 weeks (time of primary end point) and end of treatment was assessed with linear regression models adjusted for baseline values, intracavity obstruction, and baseline atrial fibrillation.
RESULTS: Among 517 participants (mean±SD: age, 55±16 years; 54% female, 75% White, 13% Asian), mean baseline LV ejection fraction was 68±4% with abnormal measures of diastolic function. Compared with placebo, aficamten decreased LV ejection fraction (-4.6% [-5.5, -3.6]; P<0.001) at 36 weeks and increased LV volumes. Aficamten improved measures of diastolic function, including lateral e' and septal e' velocities, at 36 weeks (0.9 cm/s [0.6, 1.2] and 0.7 cm/s [0.4, 0.9], respectively; P<0.001 for both) and at end of treatment (0.9 cm/s [0.5, 1.2] and 0.9 cm/s [0.6, 1.1], respectively; P<0.001 for both) and septal E/e' by end of treatment (-1.4 [-2.1, -0.6]; P<0.001, respectively). Peak tricuspid regurgitation velocity improved at 36 weeks (-10.4 cm/s [-19.9, -1.0]; P=0.030) with a sustained effect through end of treatment. Left atrial volume index did not significantly improve at 36 weeks (-1.3 [95% CI, -2.6, 0.04]; P=0.06) but showed a trend towards improvement with longer treatment exposure (-1.7 [-3.2, -0.3]; P=0.022). Aficamten demonstrated incremental improvements in measures of LV structure and function compared to placebo as doses were increased, with improvement in diastolic indices evident by week 2 of titration.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, aficamten improved echocardiographic measures of diastolic function. These findings suggest that the benefits of aficamten extend beyond the effects of LV outflow tract gradient reduction observed in prior studies.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06081894.

items.title: Oxygen vs Air at Birth for Moderate- to Late-Preterm Infants: The AIROPLANE Cluster Randomized Crossover Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The optimal initial fraction of inspired oxygen (Fio2) for delivery room resuscitation of neonates born at 32 to 35 weeks' gestation is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To compare outcomes for neonates born at 32 to 35 weeks' gestation when initiating resuscitation with Fio2 0.30 vs 0.21.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Unblinded, cluster randomized crossover trial in 26 Australian maternity hospitals, including tertiary, nontertiary, metropolitan, regional, public, and private sites, using a waiver of informed consent. All neonates born at participating sites at 32 to 35 weeks' gestation without known major congenital anomalies who commenced respiratory support within 3 minutes of birth were enrolled from December 2022 to September 2025, with final follow-up in March 2026. Statistical analysis was conducted on October 29, 2025.
INTERVENTION: Sites were randomly assigned to provide initial Fio2 of either 0.30 or 0.21 during the first 3 minutes of delivery room respiratory support. Sites crossed over to provide the alternative initial Fio2 halfway through their recruitment period.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was ongoing respiratory support when leaving the delivery room. Twelve secondary outcomes evaluated delivery room treatments and respiratory support until discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 1818 eligible newborns (mean gestational age, 34.1 weeks; mean birth weight, 2165 g; 44.7% female) were included. Ongoing respiratory support when leaving the delivery room occurred in 700 of 964 newborns (72.6%) randomized to receive Fio2 0.30 and 626 of 854 newborns (73.3%) randomized to receive Fio2 0.21 (risk difference, -0.83 [95% CI, -4.33 to 2.67]). Of the 12 secondary outcomes, 10 were not significantly different between newborns randomized to receive Fio2 0.30 vs 0.21, while 2 were. Newborns randomized to receive Fio2 0.30 were less likely to receive higher levels of support in the delivery room, including noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (606 of 964 [62.9%] vs 560 of 854 [65.6%]), endotracheal or supraglottic airway ventilation (20 of 964 [2.1%] vs 24 of 854 [2.8%]), or cardiac compressions or epinephrine (19 of 964 [2.0%] vs 25 of 854 [2.9%]; proportional odds ratio, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.52-0.95]). Fewer newborns in the Fio2 0.30 group received endotracheal ventilation beyond the delivery room (61 of 959 [6.4%] vs 79 of 852 [9.3%]; risk ratio, 0.69 [95% CI, 0.47-0.91]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: For neonates born at 32 to 35 weeks' gestation, there was no difference between those commencing resuscitation with Fio2 0.30 vs Fio2 0.21 in the proportion still receiving respiratory support when leaving the delivery room.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: anzctr.org.au Identifier: ACTRN12621001267842.

items.title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes.
items.abstract: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. This accumulation is explained by inadequate insulin-mediated interaction between AKT and Miro1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT02977442), we show that exercise training relieves skeletal muscle Miro1 accumulation while improving insulin sensitivity in patients with T2D. Muscle-specific Miro1 deletion improves oxidative capacity and insulin sensitivity in mice and cells. Taken together, these data support a key regulatory role for skeletal muscle Miro1 in the pathophysiology of T2D. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02977442.

items.title: Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression.
items.abstract: Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group (p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

items.title: Vascular Risk Factors and Late-Onset Epilepsy.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Late-onset epilepsy (LOE; onset at age ≥65 years) is increasingly recognized in older adults and may be associated with vascular risk.
OBJECTIVE: To identify vascular risk factors (VRFs) associated with incident LOE in older adults.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This study is an individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 US population-based prospective cohort studies (the Epilepsy-Cog Study). In 5 cohorts linked to Medicare for epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began when a participant had accrued 2 years of continuous fee-for-service enrollment and was 65 years of age or older and extended to the end of continuous enrollment. Claims linkage covered 1991-2018 in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC), 1992-2019 in the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), 2000-2019 in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), 2000-2020 in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study (REGARDS), and 1999-2019 in the Washington Heights/Inwood Columbia Aging Project (WHICAP). In the Northern Manhattan Study (NOMAS), which was not Medicare linked and used cohort-based epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began at cohort entry in 1993-2008 and extended to 2024. Data analysis was completed in January 2026.
EXPOSURES: Sociodemographic characteristics and VRFs assessed by self-report, examinations, laboratory measures, and medication use.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was incident LOE. Associations between risk factors and incident LOE were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios.
RESULTS: From 43 753 participants in Epilepsy-Cog, 551 participants with prevalent epilepsy and 945 with no follow-up after Epilepsy-Cog baseline were excluded. Among 42 257 participants (mean [SD] age, 71.4 [6.9] years; 23 383 [56.0%] female) followed up for a mean (SD) of 9.3 (6.2) years, 1500 participants (3.5%) developed LOE (3.8 per 1000 person-years). In fully adjusted models, LOE risk was higher with current smoking (HR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.18-1.64), hypertension (HR = 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.31), diabetes (HR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.25-1.62), chronic kidney disease (HR = 1.29; 95% CI, 1.13-1.48), history of stroke (HR = 1.99; 95% CI, 1.63-2.43), and apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (1 ε4 allele: HR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.07-1.39; 2 ε4 alleles: HR = 1.84; 95% CI, 1.36-2.50). Associations of VRFs with LOE were similar across age, sex, and race and ethnicity subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this pooled analysis of 6 US cohorts, multiple VRFs and a history of stroke were associated with incident LOE. These findings suggest that LOE may reflect the underlying burden of brain vascular disease.
